note: Declarative, vendor-neutral control checks. Each check names an asset type and the normalized signals it needs; any connector whose capability surface exposes a probe emitting those signals for that asset type can satisfy it. Adding a control here requires no connector or policy-engine code. Crosswalk references are working mappings — confirm against official framework texts before a formal audit.

checks.title: Root account MFA enforced
checks.pass_reason: Root account has MFA enabled.
checks.fail_reason: Root account does NOT have MFA enabled — full account compromise is one password away.
checks.remediation: Enable a hardware or virtual MFA device on the root user, then store the recovery codes in the organisation's break-glass vault.

checks.title: No root account access keys
checks.pass_reason: No programmatic access keys exist for the root account.
checks.fail_reason: Root account has active access keys — these bypass MFA and cannot be scoped.
checks.remediation: Delete all root access keys and replace their use with a scoped IAM role.

checks.title: Password policy minimum length
checks.pass_reason: Account password policy requires at least 14 characters.
checks.fail_reason: Account password policy allows passwords shorter than 14 characters.
checks.remediation: Set the account password policy minimum length to 14 or more.

checks.title: Password reuse prevention
checks.pass_reason: Account password policy prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords.
checks.fail_reason: Account password policy permits reusing recent passwords.
checks.remediation: Set password reuse prevention to 24 in the account password policy.

checks.title: Password complexity requirements
checks.expression: password_requires_symbols == true and password_requires_numbers == true and password_requires_uppercase == true and password_requires_lowercase == true
checks.pass_reason: Account password policy enforces symbols, numbers, and mixed case.
checks.fail_reason: Account password policy is missing one or more complexity requirements.
checks.remediation: Enable symbol, number, uppercase and lowercase requirements in the account password policy.

checks.title: Access keys rotated within 90 days
checks.pass_reason: All access keys for this principal were rotated within 90 days.
checks.fail_reason: This principal has an access key older than 90 days.
checks.remediation: Rotate the access key, update any consumer of it, then delete the superseded key.

checks.title: No inline IAM policies on principals
checks.pass_reason: Principal has no inline policies; permissions are managed centrally.
checks.fail_reason: Principal has an inline policy, which bypasses centrally reviewed managed policies.
checks.remediation: Move the inline policy into a managed policy attached via a group or role.

checks.title: No directly attached administrator policy
checks.pass_reason: Principal does not hold AdministratorAccess directly.
checks.fail_reason: Principal has AdministratorAccess attached directly, defeating least privilege.
checks.remediation: Detach AdministratorAccess and grant the narrowest role that satisfies the principal's actual usage.

checks.title: At most one active access key per principal
checks.pass_reason: Principal has at most one active access key.
checks.fail_reason: Principal has more than one active access key, widening the credential blast radius.
checks.remediation: Delete the unused access key; keep a second key only transiently during a rotation.

checks.title: Object storage encrypted with managed keys
checks.pass_reason: Bucket uses KMS-managed encryption at rest.
checks.fail_reason: Bucket does not use KMS-managed encryption, so key access cannot be audited or revoked.
checks.remediation: Set the bucket's default encryption to SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key.

checks.title: Object storage requires TLS in transit
checks.pass_reason: Bucket policy denies requests that do not use TLS.
checks.fail_reason: Bucket accepts plaintext requests — data can be read in transit.
checks.remediation: Add a bucket policy statement denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false.

checks.title: Object storage versioning enabled
checks.pass_reason: Bucket versioning is enabled, so overwrites and deletions are recoverable.
checks.fail_reason: Bucket versioning is disabled — an accidental or malicious overwrite is unrecoverable.
checks.remediation: Enable versioning on the bucket and pair it with a lifecycle rule to bound storage cost.

checks.title: Object storage access logging enabled
checks.pass_reason: Bucket access logging is enabled.
checks.fail_reason: Bucket access logging is disabled — object reads leave no audit trail.
checks.remediation: Enable server access logging to a dedicated, restricted log bucket.

checks.title: Object storage retention lifecycle configured
checks.pass_reason: Bucket has a lifecycle configuration governing retention.
checks.fail_reason: Bucket has no lifecycle configuration, so retention limits are unenforced.
checks.remediation: Add a lifecycle rule expiring or transitioning objects per the data retention schedule.

checks.title: Audit trail covers all regions
checks.pass_reason: A multi-region audit trail is active.
checks.fail_reason: No multi-region audit trail — activity in unmonitored regions is invisible.
checks.remediation: Enable a multi-region CloudTrail trail so no region is left unlogged.

checks.title: Audit log file validation enabled
checks.pass_reason: Audit log file integrity validation is enabled.
checks.fail_reason: Audit log file validation is disabled — tampering with logs would be undetectable.
checks.remediation: Enable log file validation on the trail so digest files can prove log integrity.

checks.title: Audit trail encrypted with managed keys
checks.pass_reason: Audit trail logs are encrypted with a managed key.
checks.fail_reason: Audit trail logs are not encrypted with a managed key.
checks.remediation: Configure the trail to encrypt log files with a customer-managed KMS key.

checks.title: Audit trail streamed to monitoring
checks.pass_reason: Audit trail is streamed to a log monitoring service for alerting.
checks.fail_reason: Audit trail is stored but not streamed for monitoring — nothing alerts on it.
checks.remediation: Send the trail to CloudWatch Logs and attach metric filters for high-risk API calls.

checks.title: Instance metadata service requires session tokens
checks.pass_reason: Instance requires IMDSv2 session tokens.
checks.fail_reason: Instance allows IMDSv1, which turns any SSRF into credential theft.
checks.remediation: Set the instance metadata options to require HTTP tokens (IMDSv2).

checks.title: Compute instances not directly internet-exposed
checks.pass_reason: Instance has no public IP; it is reachable only through controlled ingress.
checks.fail_reason: Instance has a public IP, exposing it directly to the internet.
checks.remediation: Move the instance to a private subnet behind a load balancer or NAT gateway.

checks.title: Compute instance detailed monitoring enabled
checks.pass_reason: Detailed monitoring is enabled on the instance.
checks.fail_reason: Detailed monitoring is disabled, reducing detection fidelity to 5-minute granularity.
checks.remediation: Enable detailed monitoring so anomalies surface within one minute.

checks.title: Block storage encrypted at rest
checks.pass_reason: Block storage volume is encrypted at rest.
checks.fail_reason: Block storage volume is NOT encrypted at rest.
checks.remediation: Snapshot the volume, create an encrypted copy, and replace the unencrypted volume.

checks.title: Managed database encrypted at rest
checks.pass_reason: Database storage is encrypted at rest.
checks.fail_reason: Database storage is NOT encrypted at rest.
checks.remediation: Restore the instance from a snapshot into an encrypted instance; encryption cannot be enabled in place.

checks.title: Managed database not publicly accessible
checks.pass_reason: Database is not publicly accessible.
checks.fail_reason: Database is publicly accessible from the internet.
checks.remediation: Set the instance to private and reach it through a bastion, VPN, or private endpoint.

checks.title: Managed database backup retention
checks.pass_reason: Database retains at least 7 days of automated backups.
checks.fail_reason: Database backup retention is under 7 days, narrowing the recovery window.
checks.remediation: Raise the automated backup retention period to at least 7 days.

checks.title: Managed database high availability
checks.pass_reason: Database is deployed across multiple availability zones.
checks.fail_reason: Database is single-AZ — a zone failure takes it offline with no automatic failover.
checks.remediation: Convert the instance to a Multi-AZ deployment.

checks.title: Managed database deletion protection
checks.pass_reason: Database has deletion protection enabled.
checks.fail_reason: Database can be deleted without an additional safeguard.
checks.remediation: Enable deletion protection on the database instance.

checks.title: Managed database automatic minor patching
checks.pass_reason: Database applies minor version security patches automatically.
checks.fail_reason: Database does not auto-apply minor patches, so known CVEs persist until manual action.
checks.remediation: Enable auto minor version upgrade and set a maintenance window.

checks.title: Managed database log export enabled
checks.pass_reason: Database exports logs to the central log service.
checks.fail_reason: Database logs are not exported, so database activity is outside central audit.
checks.remediation: Enable CloudWatch log exports for the engine's audit, error and slow-query logs.

checks.title: Managed database uses centralized authentication
checks.pass_reason: Database authenticates via central IAM rather than static credentials.
checks.fail_reason: Database relies on static passwords instead of central identity.
checks.remediation: Enable IAM database authentication and migrate application connections to token auth.

checks.title: Administrative SSH not open to the internet
checks.pass_reason: No rule exposes SSH (22) to 0.0.0.0/0.
checks.fail_reason: Security group exposes SSH (22) to the entire internet.
checks.remediation: Restrict port 22 to the bastion or corporate CIDR, or replace direct SSH with session manager.

checks.title: Administrative RDP not open to the internet
checks.pass_reason: No rule exposes RDP (3389) to 0.0.0.0/0.
checks.fail_reason: Security group exposes RDP (3389) to the entire internet.
checks.remediation: Restrict port 3389 to the bastion or corporate CIDR.

checks.title: No unrestricted inbound network rules
checks.pass_reason: Security group has no ingress rule open to the whole internet.
checks.fail_reason: Security group has at least one ingress rule open to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
checks.remediation: Replace the open CIDR with the narrowest source range the workload actually needs.

checks.title: Encryption key rotation enabled
checks.pass_reason: Automatic annual key rotation is enabled.
checks.fail_reason: Key rotation is disabled — a compromised key stays valid indefinitely.
checks.remediation: Enable automatic key rotation on the customer-managed key.

checks.title: Network flow logging enabled
checks.pass_reason: Network flow logs are active for this network.
checks.fail_reason: Network flow logs are not active — lateral movement would leave no network record.
checks.remediation: Enable VPC flow logs delivering to a restricted log destination.

checks.title: Continuous threat detection enabled
checks.pass_reason: Managed threat detection is enabled for the account.
checks.fail_reason: Managed threat detection is not enabled — malicious activity is undetected.
checks.remediation: Enable GuardDuty in every active region and route findings to the security queue.

checks.title: Configuration change recording enabled
checks.pass_reason: Configuration recording is active for the account.
checks.fail_reason: Configuration recording is off — configuration drift leaves no history.
checks.remediation: Turn on the AWS Config recorder with a delivery channel in every active region.

checks.title: Configuration recording covers all resource types
checks.pass_reason: Configuration recording covers all supported resource types.
checks.fail_reason: Configuration recording covers only a subset of resource types, leaving blind spots.
checks.remediation: Set the Config recording group to record all supported resource types, including global ones.
